structure.heading: Portfolio Performance, Strategic Options, and Board Decisions Requested (FY2024–FY2026E)
text_content: **Portfolio Performance, Strategic Options, and Board Decisions Requested (FY2024–FY2026E)**

FY2024 results show consolidated revenue of $12.4B with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.8%. Despite solid top-line scale and healthy cash generation, portfolio returns underperformed cost of capiatl: the portfolio delivered 8.1% ROIC in FY2024 versus a 9.5% WACC becnhmark. That spread signals value destruction under current allocation. Management has initiated stress-testing and scenario planning to identify low-return asests, quantify potential uplift from reallocation, and set clear targets to exceed WACC by the end of FY2026. Board engagement will be required to approve actions.

Management requests board approval by 2026-06-30 to divest the Legacy Hardawre unit and authorize a $750M capex program for the Digital Platforms unit (FY2025–FY2026). Options under consideration include: 1. strategic divestiture with prioritized bids; 2. operational turnaround and selective reinvestment; 3. joint venture or partial carve-out to retain upside while reducing exposure. Financail modeling shows the divest-and-redeploy path offers the hgihest probabiltiy of restoring ROIC above the 9.5% WACC within two years post-close, subject to execution and market conditions. Timing will factor tax considerations.

The board is requested to endorse a decision framework and record specific approvals: (a) mandate to execute a divestiture process for Legacy Hardware with binding approval target by 2026-06-30; (b) authorization of a $750M capex envelope for Digital Platforms spanning FY2025–FY2026; (c) contingency routing for proceeds prioritization toward debt reduction and targeted M&A. Management will present quarterly milestone reports, valuation assumptions, and KPI triggers (ROIC, revenue growth, EBITDA margin) and seeks board endorsement of this governance cadence. eDtailed legal and tax approvals will follow.

text_content: **Macro Environment and Risk Outlook (2024–2026) Informing Capital Allocation Priorities**

Consensus macro modelling for capital planning presents a Base Case and Downside Case for 2025. Global GDP growth is modeled at 2.6% for 2025E (Base Case) and 1.1% for 2025E (Downside Case). The detla reflects weaker advanced‑economy business investment and a China slow‑recovery scenario that compresses trade volumes and raises inventory risk. For FY2024–FY2026 plnaning this requires scenario-aligned demand curves and explicit triggers for cost and capex reprioritization. Scenario teams should map probability weightings to IMF and World Bank guidance and document reallocation thresholds.

bbl for 2025E in the Base Case, reducing short‑term fuel cost pressure versus last year but remaining above long‑term marginal cost in several supply basins. Input price volatility requires supplier contract clauses, hedging where economically justified, and indexation reviews for FY2025 procurement. The treasury should evaluate hedging under both Base and Downside price paths and quantify mipact on operating margins and working capital, and logistics planning.

Moentary policy normalization and interest‑rate paths materially affect discount rates and funding availability. The ECB deposit facility rate epaked at 4.00% in 2023 and is assumed at 3.25% for 2025E in the Base Case; similar easing paths are assumed for other major central banks in our Base Case model. This implies lower but still elevated short‑term rates versus pre‑pandemic norms, keeping bank margins healhty and borrowing costs for leveraged assets. Capital allocation should prioritize low‑duration investments, lock favorable fixed‑rate debt where possible, and stress covenant headroom.

Geopolitical fragmentation, supply‑chain re‑shoring, and elevated sovereign debt trajectories increase tail‑risk probabilities through 2026 and require explicit capital governance adjustments. Our recommended priorities: 1. Preserve liquidity buffer sufficient for 18 months of operating cash flow under the 1.1% 2025E Downside Case; 2. Defer non‑strategic M&A where payback exceeds 6 years under Base Case discount rates; 3. Accelerate digital and resilience capex that reduce variable opex. The board should endorse these guardrails and aprpove trigger‑based reallocations tied to GDP, oil, and rate thresholds and reviewed quarterly thereafter.

Board Strategy Update: Portfolio Rebalance and Capital Discipline Plan
Ref: STR-26-041 | Date: 22 February 2026 | From: Elena Marquez, Chief Strategy & Transformation Officer

Section Macroeconomic Context and Operating Environment
Global conditions entering FY2026 remain characterized by elevated interest rates, uneven GDP growth across North America and the EU, and sustained input cost volatility in energy and specialty materials. Central bank guidance suggests only gradual rate normalization, extending pressure on financing costs and customer capital budgets. Geopolitical friction in key sourcing corridors has increased lead-time variability, requiring higher working capital buffers. In this context, our strategic posture must emphasize resilience, margin protection, and selective growth in structurally advantaged segments.

Section Portfolio Performance Overview
For FY2025, consolidated revenue grew 3.1% to $4.8B, while adjusted EBITDA margin declined 120 basis points to 18.4%, primarily due to underperformance in the Industrial Components and Legacy Systems units. In contrast, the Digital Platforms and Advanced Services businesses delivered 11% organic growth and 24% EBITDA margins, with recurring revenue now representing 46% of total sales. Total shareholder return over the trailing 24 months has lagged the peer median by 380 basis points, reflecting both margin compression and portfolio complexity. These trends underscore the need to rebalance toward higher-return, lower-risk growth platforms.

Section Strategic Choices Under Consideration
Management proposes the divestment of the Industrial Components division, representing approximately $620M in revenue but sub-scale margins and elevated cyclicality. Proceeds would be redeployed to accelerate investment in Digital Platforms, including $180M in disciplined capex over three years focused on cloud-native infrastructure and AI-enabled analytics modules. We are also evaluating two bolt-on acquisitions in the compliance automation and edge monitoring spaces, with combined enterprise value estimated at $410M and clear cost and cross-sell synergies. These actions are designed to lift group EBITDA margin above 21% by FY2028 while reducing earnings volatility.

Section Capital Allocation Framework
Under the proposed plan, net leverage would be maintained within a 1.8x–2.2x EBITDA corridor, preserving investment-grade metrics. Share repurchases would be paused through FY2027 to prioritize strategic M&A and targeted deleveraging. Capital expenditures will be subject to a minimum 18% IRR hurdle rate and stage-gated governance reviews. This disciplined framework aims to restore TSR momentum while maintaining flexibility under persistent macro uncertainty.

Section Board Actions Requested
We seek board endorsement to initiate a formal sale process for Industrial Components in Q2 2026 and to authorize preliminary diligence on the two identified acquisition targets. Approval is also requested for the revised three-year capital plan and updated leverage policy. Management will return in September 2026 with a detailed transaction update and refined synergy capture roadmap. Timely approval will enable execution before further market normalization compresses valuation differentials.
